design_rationale: The study explicitly states that after surgery patients were randomly assigned to cast or removable functional-brace treatment, although the sequence-generation method is not described.

domain_judgments.rationale: Random assignment was stated and measured baseline characteristics showed no statistically significant differences, but neither sequence generation nor allocation concealment was reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: After operation, patients were randomly assigned to one of the two modes of treatment.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and treating staff could not be blinded to cast versus removable brace and exercise instructions, and the analysis excluded five randomized patients rather than clearly using intention-to-treat, although no intervention-related deviations were reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: This left 55 patients who completed the follow-up examinations and the SF-36 questionnaire.

domain_judgments.rationale: Five of 60 randomized participants (8.3%) did not complete follow-up, and attrition by assigned group and sensitivity analyses addressing possible bias were not reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Of the 60 patients entered into the study, one moved abroad, one developed multiple sclerosis with severe progression of his disease and three were lost to follow-up.

domain_judgments.rationale: The main functional score included subjective pain and function components and was assessed by the operating surgeon, who necessarily knew whether a patient wore a cast or brace, creating substantial potential for differential measurement; return-to-work reporting was also not adjusted for type of work or comorbidities.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The limitations of the study include the fact that the operating surgeon performed the follow-up rating scores.

domain_judgments.rationale: No preregistration or prespecified analysis plan is reported, and numerous time points and SF-36 subscales were analyzed, leaving scope for selective emphasis among eligible results, although tables and figures report many nonsignificant findings.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The SF-36 questionnaire assesses eight separate aspects of quality of health.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is high because the unblinded operating surgeon measured the partly subjective functional outcome. Additional concerns arise from unreported sequence concealment, complete-case rather than clearly intention-to-treat analysis, incompletely characterized attrition, and lack of a prespecified analysis plan.

design_rationale: The report explicitly states that, after postoperative eligibility assessment, patients were randomized to brace or plaster treatment.

domain_judgments.rationale: Random allocation was stated and fracture type appeared balanced, but the sequence-generation and allocation-concealment methods were not reported and broader baseline comparability was insufficiently described.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The patient was then randomized to brace or plaster treatment.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and care providers could not be blinded to brace versus plaster, and adherence, crossover, and intention-to-treat analysis were not explicitly reported, although all patients appear to have received the assigned programs.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All patients were given a program for self-training of mobility, muscular strength, and function (such as stair climbing). The brace group received this program immediately; the plaster group received it at 6 weeks.

domain_judgments.rationale: The results and tables account for all 30 randomized patients (15 per group) at the main 10-week and 12-month assessments, with no reported attrition; the selective three-year reassessment was supplementary and explicitly limited to nine poor-result patients.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: After 6 weeks, 6 of the 15 patients in the brace group showed failure of the syndesmotic staples, compared with one in the plaster group.

domain_judgments.rationale: ROM and isokinetic strength were measured with standardized methods across groups, but assessor blinding was not reported and subjective score outcomes could be influenced by participants' unavoidable knowledge of treatment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Special follow-up at 10 weeks and 12 months included: (1) subjective problems monitored by a modified Olerud score; (2) measurement of muscular hypotrophy of the leg and ankle swelling; (3) testing dorsiflexion and plantarflexion ROM using a standard goniometer; and (4) measurement of isokinetic dorsiflexion muscle strength using an isokinetic testing machine (Cybex).

domain_judgments.rationale: No preregistration or prespecified analysis plan was reported, while numerous outcomes, time points, angular velocities, and statistical tests created scope for selective reporting or analysis.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Common statistical analysis was performed using analysis of variance and paired and two-sample t-tests when muscle strength measurements were evaluated. Wilcoxon and Mann-Whitney rank sum tests were used when clinical results, such as ROM, were evaluated.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is judged as some concerns. The main limitations are absent details on sequence generation and allocation concealment, lack of reported blinding and intention-to-treat procedures, and no prespecified protocol despite multiple eligible outcomes and analyses; outcome completeness appears adequate.

design_rationale: Participants were explicitly allocated 1:1 by a secure web-based system using a minimisation algorithm with a random element, maintained by an independent randomisation team.

domain_judgments.rationale: The allocation sequence included a random element, was implemented through an independent secure web system, baseline data were collected before allocation, and reported baseline characteristics were generally balanced.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A secure web based system maintained by an independent randomisation team allocated participants using a minimisation algorithm with a random element and stratification by centre, operative or non-operative management, and age (≤49 v ≥50 years).

domain_judgments.rationale: Although participants and clinicians could not be blinded and some crossover occurred, co-interventions were balanced and the prespecified primary analysis appropriately retained participants in their randomized groups on an intention-to-treat basis.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Twenty three participants in the cast group (n=334) did not adhere to the treatment allocation and crossed over to the removable brace group... Seven participants in the removable brace group (n=335) did not adhere to the treatment allocation and crossed over to the cast group... [and] the planned main analysis... was on an intention-to-treat basis.

domain_judgments.rationale: Only 75% of randomized participants provided the 16-week primary outcome, with somewhat greater missingness in the cast group, although multiple-imputation sensitivity analyses and comparisons of baseline characteristics supported robustness.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Five hundred and two participants completed the primary outcome Olerud Molander ankle score score (75%) and were included in the final analysis... Missingness of the primary outcome was not evenly distributed between the groups, with more data missing in the cast group (completeness: cast group 73%; removable brace 78%).

domain_judgments.rationale: The validated self-administered functional outcome was measured identically across groups, but participants were necessarily aware of treatment allocation and their subjective reports could therefore have been influenced by that knowledge.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Blinding of participants and clinicians was not possible. All follow-up data were participant reported through postal questionnaires; no clinicians or researchers assessed outcome measures.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered, its protocol and independently approved statistical analysis plan preceded outcome analysis, and the reported primary outcome, time point, and adjusted intention-to-treat analysis match the prespecified methods.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: This study was prospectively registered on 24 July 2017... The independent trial steering committee and data and safety monitoring committee approved the statistical analysis plan.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is some concerns, driven mainly by 25% missing primary-outcome data with modest differential completeness and by the subjective participant-reported outcome in an unblinded trial. Robust randomization, intention-to-treat analysis, imputation sensitivity analyses, and prospective specification reduce concerns in the other domains.

design_rationale: The study explicitly reports 1:1 random allocation at the two-week postoperative visit using concealed, sequentially numbered, opaque, sealed envelopes.

domain_judgments.rationale: Allocation concealment was adequately described, but the method used to generate the random sequence was not reported, and the primary-outcome baseline state was imbalanced between groups despite otherwise similar baseline characteristics.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Randomization was performed by the research coordinators at the two week post operative visit by use of concealed sequentially numbered, opaque, sealed envelopes, in 1:1 ratio.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and investigators could not be blinded, adherence to the distinct rehabilitation protocols was not verified, and some eligibility/protocol violations occurred, although analysis was by intention to treat and no intervention crossovers were reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Although it would have been desirable, it was not practical to blind patients or investigators to their treatment group.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary return-to-work analysis included 90 of 97 participants employed at injury, excluding participants with loss to follow-up, missing dates, or no return by 12 months, without sensitivity analysis demonstrating that these exclusions could not bias the effect estimate.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Therefore, 90 patients with compete results were available for calculation of time to return to work.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome measures were generally appropriate and scheduled identically across groups, but research staff/investigators were unblinded, and participant-reported return to work and functional outcomes could be influenced by knowledge of assigned rehabilitation.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Patients were asked a standard set of questions by the research staff regarding their return to work and activity as well as adverse events.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although the primary and secondary outcomes were identified and a sample-size calculation was reported, no prospective registration or prespecified statistical analysis plan is provided, while multiple outcomes and time points permit selective reporting or analysis.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary outcome in this study was rate of return to work. Secondary outcome measures included ankle range of motion (ROM), ankle functional outcome scores (Olerud/Molander), health outcome scores (SF-36 Health Survey), wound complications (dehiscence, delayed healing, infection), and fracture fixation complications (fixation failure, loss of reduction, reoperation).

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is some concerns. The trial used concealed allocation and intention-to-treat analysis, but sequence generation was not described, the primary outcome was imbalanced at randomization, adherence was unverified in an unblinded trial, some primary-outcome data were excluded, and no prespecified protocol or analysis plan was reported.

design_rationale: Allocation was determined by the admitting consultant rather than a random sequence: patients under consultant A received immobilization and those under consultant B received mobilization.

domain_judgments.rationale: Treatment was completely confounded with consultant/provider, and no baseline characteristics or adjusted analysis were reported to establish comparability on prognostic factors.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All injured patients admitted under the care of consultant “A” were included to the “immobilized group” (n = 22) ... All injured patients admitted under the care of consultant “B” were included to the “mobilized group” (n = 22).

domain_judgments.domain_name: Bias due to selection of participants into the study
domain_judgments.rationale: All eligible presenting patients were reportedly included prospectively, but condition assignment depended on admission under one of two participating consultants and the relationship between the roster/admission pathway and prognosis was not evaluated.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All patients presenting to the four accident and emergency departments in our catchment area between January 15, 2001 and November 30, 2001, who fulfilled these criteria, were included in this study.

domain_judgments.rationale: The two postoperative interventions were clearly defined at assignment and were unlikely to be misclassified.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The immobilized group remained in cast for 6 weeks. The mobilized group was free of plaster casting.

domain_judgments.domain_name: Bias due to deviations from intended interventions
domain_judgments.rationale: The intended regimens and common weight-bearing schedule were specified, but adherence, crossovers, co-interventions, and the analysis population were not reported, while participants and treating clinicians necessarily knew treatment status.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Both groups commenced partial weight bearing at 4 weeks and gradually progressed to full weight bearing as tolerated.

domain_judgments.rationale: Results are presented for the enrolled cohort and assessments are described as applying to all patients, but outcome-specific denominators and explicit confirmation of complete follow-up are absent.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: An independent and blinded physiotherapist assessed all patients at 6 and 12 weeks post-surgery.

domain_judgments.rationale: Validated or standardized outcome methods were applied similarly, and the physiotherapist was blinded for 6- and 12-week functional assessments, but early pain and satisfaction were self-reported by participants aware of treatment and the clinical/radiologic examiner was explicitly nonblinded.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A nonblinded independent examiner assessed each patient, both clinically and radiologically.

domain_judgments.domain_name: Bias in selection of the reported result
domain_judgments.rationale: No protocol or prespecified analysis plan was reported despite multiple outcomes, time points, and component measurements, leaving scope for selective reporting or analysis.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Patients were assessed for pain, satisfaction, range of movements according to Lindsjo et al. and Olerud’s & Molander’s functional outcome and radiologic appearance postoperatively.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is serious because intervention assignment was determined by consultant, making treatment inseparable from provider effects, with no reported baseline comparability or confounding adjustment. Additional moderate concerns involve selection, adherence/missing-data reporting, outcome measurement, and selective reporting.

design_rationale: Participants were explicitly assigned in a 1:1:1 ratio using a computerized random-number generator with block randomization.

domain_judgments.rationale: The sequence was computer-generated with blocked 1:1:1 allocation, allocation was reported as concealed, and no statistically significant baseline imbalances were identified.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Patients were randomized using a computerized random number generator with an allocation ratio of 1:1:1 in blocks of 21 patients.

domain_judgments.rationale: Patients and clinicians were unblinded, three participants crossed over because of cast irritation, and adherence was uncertain, although the analysis followed intention-to-treat and the crossover was limited.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The study was limited by the fact that there was no blinding of patients, treating physicians or outcome assessors; however, it is unclear whether blinding is truly necessary in this pragmatic trial.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome availability was 88% at three months and 86% at one year, and only available cases were analyzed without correction or evidence that missingness could not bias results.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: At 3 months and 1 year, follow-up information was available for 88% and 86% of the subjects, respectively, for all outcomes. We performed an available case analysis, and no corrections for loss to follow-up were applied.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary functional outcome was patient-reported and could plausibly be influenced by participants' unavoidable knowledge of their visibly different postoperative regimen, while outcome assessors were also unblinded.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The study was limited by the fact that there was no blinding of patients, treating physicians or outcome assessors.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was registered and methods and analyses were prespecified, but the significance boundary was chosen post hoc after early termination, creating some potential for data-dependent reporting or interpretation despite use of a conservative boundary.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The protocol pre-specified our methods and statistical analysis plan, except for the statistical significance bound, for which we decided post hoc to use the conservative O’Brien-Fleming approach.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is high because the primary patient-reported functional outcome could plausibly have been influenced by participants' knowledge of the assigned postoperative regimen. Additional concerns arise from incomplete outcome data analyzed as available cases, limited crossover/nonadherence information, and a post hoc interim-analysis significance boundary.

design_rationale: This was a prospective randomized trial in which 100 postoperative patients were allocated to cast or functional-brace treatment using sealed envelopes.

domain_judgments.rationale: Allocation used sealed envelopes and groups were broadly similar at baseline, but the random-sequence generation method and whether envelopes were opaque, sequentially numbered, and securely concealed were not reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Postoperatively, the patients were randomly allocated, with use of sealed envelopes, to treatment with either a cast or a functional ankle brace for the first six weeks after the operation.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and treating personnel necessarily knew the visibly different postoperative treatments, and although protocols were clearly specified, adherence, crossover, and an intention-to-treat analysis were not explicitly reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The patients managed with conventional treatment wore a below-the-knee plaster cast... The other group was managed with a functional Air-Stirrup ankle brace... Daily active and passive range-of-motion exercises... were encouraged immediately postoperatively.

domain_judgments.rationale: All 100 participants were assessed through six weeks, but 12% were missing at two years (16% cast versus 8% brace), and no sensitivity analysis established that the long-term results were robust to this differential attrition.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A total of twelve patients were lost to follow-up before the two-year follow-up examination... forty-two and forty-six at the two-year follow-up examination.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcomes were measured consistently with standardized clinical measures and validated scales by an independent physician, but assessor blinding to treatment assignment was not reported and some outcomes were participant-reported and therefore unblinded.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: To limit the bias inherent in all clinical examinations and manual tests, the follow-up examinations and rating scores at twelve and fifty-two weeks and at two years were performed by the same independent physician who had not been involved in the actual treatment of any of the patients.

domain_judgments.rationale: No preregistration or prespecified statistical analysis plan was reported, while numerous subjective, clinical, radiographic, functional, and time-point-specific outcomes offered scope for selective reporting, although the paper presents detailed results for the stated measures.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The recovery of the patients was assessed clinically with use of subjective, objective, and radiographic evaluation criteria at two, six, twelve, and fifty-two weeks and at two years postoperatively.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is judged as some concerns. The trial was randomized and largely well reported, but sequence generation and allocation concealment details were incomplete, blinding and intention-to-treat analysis were not established, two-year attrition was differential, and no prespecified protocol or analysis plan was available.
